# A conditional two-contact lemma for inverse-arm localization

This is a proved one-dimensional contact statement. It does not prove existence of a profile extremizer, multiplier qualification, or the required complementarity certificate. Those are separate outstanding dependencies of the proposed profile localization.

Let J be an open bounded interval contained in (0,infinity). Let A be finite concave on J, with curvature measure mu=-A''>=0. Let w:J->(0,infinity) be continuous. Suppose H is twice continuously differentiable, has one fixed sign on J, and

    H''(v)=w(v)[a v+b+c A(v)],
    supp(mu) subset {H=0}.

If c is nonzero, then mu is supported on at most two points of J. If c=0 and the affine function a v+b is not identically zero, the same conclusion holds. The fully degenerate case a=b=c=0 is deliberately excluded.

## Proof

Replace H and (a,b,c) by their negatives if needed, so H>=0. Put B(v)=a v+b+c A(v). It is convex or concave when c is nonzero, and affine otherwise. Because w>0, H'' has the same signs as B.

If x<y are zeros of H and H is not identically zero between them, there are three ordered points of (x,y) where H'' has signs positive, negative, positive. Indeed H'(x)=H'(y)=0, since these are interior minima. A positive value of H between its zero endpoint values gives an earlier point of positive derivative and a later point of negative derivative, by the mean value theorem. Apply the mean value theorem again between x and the positive derivative, between the positive and negative derivatives, and between the negative derivative and y. Consequently B has the same three signs at three ordered points.

A concave B cannot have signs positive, negative, positive: its middle value is bounded below by the positive chord between the outer points. Thus in this case H's zero set is connected. A convex B cannot have signs negative, positive, negative. Three distinct components of H's zero set would supply two successive gaps. Applying the preceding derivative argument on both gaps supplies signs positive, negative, positive, negative, positive; the middle three signs contradict convexity. Hence in the convex case the zero set has at most two components. The same argument applies to affine B, which is both convex and concave.

If a component contains a nontrivial interval, H vanishes there, hence B vanishes there. For c nonzero this makes A affine there, so mu gives the interior of the component zero mass. Moreover a convex B that vanishes on an interval is nonnegative everywhere on J, and a concave such B is nonpositive everywhere. This follows directly from monotonicity of its one-sided slopes. In the convex case H''>=0, so the zero set of the nonnegative convex H is connected. In the concave case H''<=0; a nonnegative concave H with an interior zero is identically zero on J. Thus an interval component cannot coexist with a second component.

It follows that either the zero set consists of at most two isolated points, or it is one interval on whose interior mu vanishes. In the latter case only its at most two endpoints lying in J can carry mu. If H vanishes identically, then B vanishes identically, and c nonzero makes A affine on J, so mu=0 there. When c=0 and B is nonzero affine, an interval zero component or H identically zero is impossible. In every admitted case mu is supported on at most two points. QED.

## Conditional application to the profile problem

With finitely many fixed slope intersections, the inverse-arm Lagrangian load between thresholds has the form v^(m-2)[a v+b+c A(v)]. If an attained variational problem supplies a signed dual contact function H with H'' equal to that load and with curvature supported on its zeros, this lemma bounds each arm's interior curvature support by two points per nondegenerate threshold interval. Threshold points themselves must still be counted separately. Intervals with identically zero load and absent quadratic coefficient require another argument; no genericity or automatic multiplier existence is assumed.

# A conditional two-contact lemma for inverse-arm localization

**Two-interior-atom curvature contact lemma**

Let J be a bounded open subinterval of (0,infinity), let A be a finite concave function on J, and write mu=-A'' for its distributional curvature measure. Let w be continuous and strictly positive on J and H in C^2(J) have one sign with supp(mu) contained in {H=0}. If H''(v)=w(v)(a v+b+c A(v)) and (a,b,c)!=(0,0,0), then mu is supported on at most two interior points. The assertion includes interval contacts and accumulating zero sets, but assumes the one-sign potential and complementarity; it does not establish their existence.

Scope limits: Conditional on the one-sign potential and complementarity. Does not itself establish multiplier existence. Coefficient nondegeneracy, not a literally nonzero evaluated load, is the corrected condition.
